# iliad-039 — new renderings (6.332–439)

Rows in the form of the conventions table. Every row here is a choice this part makes that the table does not already fix; where a row follows the table or the Odyssey for a new form, the last column says so. No row departs from a published rendering. The packet's repeated lines (6.332, 6.333, 6.334, 6.342, 6.359, 6.369, 6.406) take the packet's English; 6.333–334 and 6.342 stand inside differently cut units, so only the wording is reused.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| δᾶερ (vocative, 6.344, 6.355) | "Husband’s-brother" | "My husband’s brother" | "brother-in-law" (turned down at δαὴρ, 3.180, because it also covers a sister's husband), "brother", "dear brother"; δαήρ keeps the English of 3.180, with "my" added for the address |
| ἐμεῖο κυνός (Helen of herself, 6.344, 6.356) | "of me, a dog" | "a dog like me" / "me, a dog" | "bitch", "cur", "hound", "wretch"; κύων as abuse is "dog" (Odyssey 17.248), and the note says it also means shameless |
| κακομηχάνου (6.344) | "evil-contriving" | "a contriver of evil" | "scheming", "plotting" (turned down in the Odyssey table for δολοφρονέων), "evil-minded"; κακός "evil", μηχανάομαι "contrive" |
| ὀκρυοέσσης (6.344; ὀκρυόεις rare, traditional gloss) | "chilling" | "a chilling thing" | "horrible", "dreadful" (reserved for δεινός), "icy"; the note says the gloss is the traditional one |
| ὥς μ’ ὄφελ’ … οἴχεσθαι προφέρουσα κακὴ ἀνέμοιο θύελλα (6.345–346) | "Would that … an evil storm-blast had gone off bearing me forth" | "If only … an evil storm-blast had carried me off" | "hurricane", "tempest", "whirlwind"; θύελλα keeps "storm-blast" (Odyssey 5.292), ὡς ὄφελ’ keeps "Would that" / "If only" (3.428, 4.315) |
| ἀπόερσε (6.348; rare aorist) | "swept away" | "would have swept away" | "washed away", "carried away", "drowned"; the aorist after a wish is put in the conditional in `i` only |
| τεκμήραντο (6.349) | "fixed" | "have fixed" | "ordained", "decreed" (turned down at τεκμαίρομαι, Odyssey 7.317), "devised"; follows the table |
| ὤφελλον … εἶναι ἄκοιτις (6.350) | "would that I were wife" | "if only I had been the wife" | "I ought to have been", "I should have been"; follows αἴθ’ ὄφελες "If only" (1.415), ὤφελλον being the doubled-λ form of ὀφείλω, not ὀφέλλω "increase" |
| νέμεσιν … αἴσχεα πόλλ’ ἀνθρώπων (6.351) | "resentment and the many shames of men" | "men’s resentment and their many shames" | "disgrace", "reproach" for αἴσχεα (kept for ὄνειδος); follows νέμεσις "resentment" (2.296) and αἴσχεα "the shames" (3.242) |
| ἔμπεδοι φρένες (6.352) | "wits firm" | "wits … firm" | "steady", "sound", "steadfast"; follows the Odyssey table's φρένες ἔμπεδοι (18.215) |
| ἐπαυρήσεσθαι (6.353; the object left unsaid) | "have the benefit of it" | "have the benefit of it" | "reap", "enjoy", "taste" (as at 1.410); the table's row, with "it" supplied and the note saying the Greek gives no object |
| τῷδ’ ἐπὶ δίφρῳ (6.354) | "on this stool" | "on this stool" | "chair" (reserved for θρόνος), "seat" (reserved for κλισμός); follows δίφρον of a seat "stool" (3.424) |
| πόνος … φρένας ἀμφιβέβηκεν (6.355) | "toil … has come around your wits" | "toil has come around your wits" | "has surrounded", "has taken hold of", "weighs on"; ἀμφιβαίνω "go round", ἀμφὶ … βαῖνε "strode round" (5.299) |
| ἀοίδιμοι (6.358; rare, "sung of") | "sung-of" | "a subject of song" | "famous in song", "celebrated", "a theme for singers"; ἀοιδή "song" in both; no earlier unit has the word |
| κακὸν μόρον (6.357) | "an evil doom" | "an evil doom" | "evil fate" (reserved for μοῖρα, αἶσα), "evil portion"; μόρος keeps "doom" (Odyssey 9.61, 11.409) |
| φιλέουσά περ (6.360) | "loving me though you do" | "though you love me" | "though you are kind to me", "for all your kindness"; φιλέω "love", the note says it includes friendly treatment |
| κάθιζ’ (καθίζω, transitive, 6.360) | "Do not seat me" | "Do not make me sit down" | "Do not sit me", "Do not ask me to sit"; καθίζω "make sit" |
| ἐπέσσυται … ἐπαμύνω (6.361) | "is rushing on … come to the defence of" | "is already rushing on … come to the defence of" | "is set", "is eager" (kept for μεμαώς), "defend", "help" (kept for ἀρήγω); follows ἐπάμυνον "come to my defence" (5.685) |
| ποθὴν ἔχουσιν (6.362) | "feel the lack of me" | "feel the lack of me" | "miss me" (kept for ποθέω, 2.703), "long for me", "have longing for"; follows ποθή "the lack of Achilles" (1.240) |
| ὄρνυθι τοῦτον (6.363) | "rouse this man" | "rouse him" | "stir", "urge"; ὄρνυμι "rouse" (the table) |
| καταμάρψῃ (6.364) | "overtake" | "overtakes" | "catch" in `l`, "seize", "arrest"; follows κατέμαρπτε "overtook" (5.65) |
| οἰκῆας (6.366) | "household servants" | "household servants" | "kinsmen", "slaves", "people of the house"; follows the Odyssey table's οἰκῆες (17.533); kept apart from δμῶες / δμῳαί |
| ὑπότροπος ἵξομαι (6.367) | "come back … returning" | "come back" | "return home" (kept for νοστέω), "arrive back"; ὑπότροπος "returning" (Odyssey 20.332) |
| δαμόωσιν (6.368) | "subdue" | "overcome" | "tame", "conquer" (reserved for νικάω), "kill"; δαμάζω "subdue" / "overcome" (5.106, 5.391) |
| γοόωσά τε μυρομένη τε (6.373) | "sobbing and mourning" | "sobbing and mourning" | "weeping" (kept for κλαίω and δάκρυ χέω), "wailing" (kept for οἰμώζω), "lamenting" (kept for γόος "lament"); γοάω keeps "sobbing" (Odyssey 4.721, ἁδινὸν γοόωσα), and μύρομαι is given "mourning" because the three nearest words are taken |
| ἐφεστήκει (6.373) | "was standing on" | "was standing on" | "had taken her stand", "stood"; the pluperfect of ἐφίστημι in the sense of the state, as in the Odyssey's "stand by" |
| τέτμεν (6.374; old aorist) | "came upon" | "found" | "met" (reserved for ἀντάω "meet"), "encountered"; εὗρ’ (6.371) is "find", so the two verbs are kept apart in `l` |
| μετὰ δὲ δμῳῇσιν ἔειπεν (6.375) | "among the maidservants spoke" | "spoke among the maids" | "to the maidservants", "addressed" (reserved for προσέφη); follows the Odyssey table's δμῳαί "maidservants" / "maids" (6.69, 6.99) and the pattern μετέειπε "spoke among" |
| νημερτέα μυθήσασθε (6.376) | "tell me unerring things" | "tell me unerring things" | "tell me the truth" (turned down in the table for νημερτέα εἰπεῖν, 11.96), "tell me truly" (νημερτές, 1.514), "without fail"; the Odyssey's English |
| γαλόων · εἰνατέρων (6.378, 6.383) | "her husband’s sisters" · "the wives of her husband’s brothers" | "my sisters" (Hector) / "your sisters" (the housekeeper) · "my / your brothers’ … wives" | "sisters-in-law" (the table turns it down for γάλως, 3.122), "his sisters"; both words are named from Andromache's side, and `i` puts them into the speaker's mouth |
| ἐξοίχεται (6.379, 6.384) | "has gone out" | "has gone out" | "has left", "is away", "is out"; ἐξοίχομαι "go out", serving all three places |
| ἐς Ἀθηναίης (6.379, 6.384; ellipsis) | "to Athena’s" | "to Athena’s temple" | "to Athena", "to the shrine of Athena"; the Greek leaves out the word "temple", which `i` supplies |
| ἐϋπλόκαμοι Τρῳαί (6.380, 6.385) | "fine-plaited Trojan women" | "fine-plaited Trojan women" | "fair-tressed" (reserved for ἐυπλοκαμῖδες), "fair-haired" (ξανθός), "well-braided"; ἐυπλόκαμος keeps "fine-plaited" (Odyssey 1.86, 5.390, 10.136) |
| δεινὴν θεὸν ἱλάσκονται (6.380, 6.385) | "appease the dread goddess" | "appease the dread goddess" | "propitiate", "placate", "worship"; ἱλάσκομαι "appease" (1.386), δεινός "dread" |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ ὀτρηρὴ ταμίη πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν (6.381, whole-line speech introduction) | "Him then in turn the brisk housekeeper addressed with a word:" | "Then the brisk housekeeper spoke to him in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "nimble", "busy", "quick" for ὀτρηρή, "stewardess", "steward" for ταμίη; πρὸς … ἔειπεν follows the table's ἦ ῥα καὶ [Name] πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν (Odyssey 19.96) |
| ἦ ῥα γυνὴ ταμίη, ὃ δ’ ἀπέσσυτο δώματος Ἕκτωρ (6.390) | "She spoke, the woman, the housekeeper, and he rushed away from the house, Hector," | "So the housekeeper spoke, and Hector rushed out of the house," | "Thus she spoke", "she finished"; follows the table's ἦ ῥα "He/She spoke" / "So he/she said" (3.337); ἀπέσσυτο "rushed away" (4.527) |
| ἀληθέα (6.382) | "true things" | "the truth" | "unerring things" (reserved for νημερτέα), "frank words", "honestly"; ἀληθής "true" |
| μάλ’ ἄνωγας (6.382) | "you so strongly bid" | "you press me so" | "you urgently bid", "you insist"; ἄνωγα "bid" (4.263, 5.899) |
| ἀφικάνει (6.388) | "arrives" | "she arrives" | "reaches", "has come to"; the present is kept in both layers |
| μαινομένῃ ἐϊκυῖα (6.389) | "like to one raging" | "like a woman out of her mind" | "like a madwoman", "raving", "frantic" (each decides the degree); μαίνομαι keeps "rage" in `l` (5.185) and `i` gives the sense, as the table does for Dionysus (6.132) |
| τιθήνη (6.389) | "the nurse" | "the nurse" | "wet-nurse", "attendant"; τιθήναι "nurses" (6.132), ἀμφίπολος "handmaid" is kept for the other woman |
| ἐϋκτιμένας ἀγυιάς (6.391) | "well-built streets" | "well-built streets" | "well-founded", "fair-built", "well-ordered"; ἐυκτίμενος keeps "well-built" (Odyssey 3.4), ἀγυιά "street" (5.642) |
| διερχόμενος μέγα ἄστυ (6.392) | "passing through the great town" | "passing through the great town" | "city" (reserved for πόλις), "crossing"; ἄστυ "town" (Odyssey), διέρχομαι "pass through" |
| πολύδωρος ἄλοχος (6.394) | "rich in gifts" | "rich in gifts" | "richly dowered", "of many gifts"; follows the Odyssey table's πολύδωρος (24.294), with the note |
| ὑπὸ Πλάκῳ ὑληέσσῃ · Θήβῃ Ὑποπλακίῃ (6.396–397) | "beneath wooded Placus" · "Hypoplacian Thebe" | "beneath wooded Placus" · "Hypoplacian Thebe" | "forested", "timbered" for ὑληέσσῃ; "Thebe under Placus" (repeats the preposition of the line before); ὕλη "forest" (5.52), the name kept as a name with the note |
| Κιλίκεσσ’ ἄνδρεσσιν ἀνάσσων (6.397) | "ruling over Cilician men" | "was lord over the Cilician men" | "king of", "commanding"; ἀνάσσω keeps "rule over" / "be lord over" (1.180) |
| ἔχεθ’ Ἕκτορι (6.398; ἔχομαι with the dative) | "was held by … Hector" | "had as his wife" (Hector) | "was married to", "belonged to", "was given to"; ἔχω "hold", and the note says the middle means "be held as wife" |
| ἀταλάφρονα (6.400; rare) | "tender-minded" | "tender-minded" | "innocent", "childlike", "playful", "light-hearted" (each decides the sense); ἀταλός "tender" (Odyssey 11.39) + φρήν "mind" |
| νήπιον αὔτως (6.400) | "an infant simply" | "a mere infant" | "just an infant", "only a baby", "helpless"; νήπιος "infant" (5.688), αὔτως "simply" (3.220) |
| ἀγαπητόν · ἀλίγκιον (6.401) | "beloved" · "like to" | "beloved" · "like" | "dear", "only" for ἀγαπητόν; "equal to", "resembling" for ἀλίγκιον; ἀγαπητός "beloved" (kept apart from φίλος "dear"), ἀλίγκιος "like" (kept apart from ἐοικώς and ἐπιείκελος) |
| καλέεσκε (6.402) | "kept calling" | "used to call" | "would call", "was called"; the iterative suffix is shown by "kept" in `l`, as at 4.233 |
| Σκαμάνδριον · Ἀστυάνακτ’ (6.402–403) | "Scamandrius" · "Astyanax" | "Scamandrius" · "Astyanax" | "Skamandrios", "Astyanact"; Latinised forms, as for the other Greek names, with the meaning of the second given in the note |
| ἐρύετο Ἴλιον (6.403) | "was guarding Ilios" | "guarded Ilios" | "defended", "warded off" (reserved for ἀμύνω), "saved"; ἐρύομαι "guard" (4.186) |
| μείδησεν … σιωπῇ (6.404) | "smiled … silent" | "smiled silently" | "smiled in silence" (σιγῇ is "in silence"), "without a word"; σιωπῇ keeps "silent" (Odyssey 7.154) |
| ἄμμορον (6.408) | "ill-fated" | "ill-fated" | "portionless", "luckless", "wretched" (reserved for δύστηνος); built on μόρος like κάμμορε "Ill-fated one" (Odyssey 5.160), the note gives the parts |
| νηπίαχον (6.408) | "childish" | "little" | "infant" (kept for νήπιος), "babyish", "foolish"; νηπίαχος "childish" (2.338); `l` repeats "child" with it, and `i` takes the sense |
| χήρη σεῦ (6.408) | "a widow bereft of you" | "a widow bereft of you" | "your widow", "widowed of you"; the genitive of what is lost |
| ἐφορμηθέντες (6.410) | "having rushed upon you" | "rushing upon you" | "attacking", "setting upon", "falling on"; ἐφορμάομαι "rush upon" (Odyssey 11.206) |
| σεῦ ἀφαμαρτούσῃ (6.411) | "having lost you" | "once I have lost you" | "bereft of you" (kept for χήρη σεῦ), "missing you", "deprived of you"; ἀφαμαρτάνω "miss, lose" |
| θαλπωρή (6.412) | "comfort" | "comfort" | "warmth", "solace", "consolation"; related to θάλπω "warm", no earlier unit has the word |
| πότμον ἐπίσπῃς (6.412) | "met your doom" | "met your doom" | "followed your fate", "gone to your fate"; ἐφέπω aorist "come upon, meet"; πότμος "doom" (4.170) |
| ἐκ … πέρσεν (6.415) | "sacked" | "sacked" | "utterly sacked", "stormed", "destroyed"; ἐκπέρθω keeps "sack" (1.19) and the tmesis is named in the note |
| ὑψίπυλον (Θήβην, 6.416) | "high-gated" | "high-gated" | "of the high gates", "tall-gated", "lofty-gated"; ὑψί "high" + πύλη "gate" |
| ἐξενάριξε (6.417; the killing already told) | "despoil" | "strip of his armour" | "kill and strip" (the table's row, where the killing is in the same verb), "plunder", "rob"; ἐξεναρίζω keeps the stripping only |
| κατέκηε σὺν ἔντεσι δαιδαλέοισιν (6.418) | "burned … with his wrought gear" | "burned … with his finely wrought gear" | "armour" (reserved for τεύχεα), "burnished", "cunning"; ἔντεα "gear" (Odyssey 23.368), δαιδαλέος "wrought" / "finely wrought" (4.135) |
| ἐπὶ σῆμ’ ἔχεεν (6.419) | "poured a tomb over" | "heaped a tomb over" | "heaped a mound", "raised a barrow", "poured a mound"; σῆμα "tomb" (2.814), χέω "pour", with "heaped" in `i` for a tomb of earth |
| πτελέας · ὀρεστιάδες (6.419–420) | "elms" · "of the mountains" | "elms" · "mountain" | "elm trees", "wych-elms" · "mountain-dwelling", "of the hills"; πτελέα "elm", ὀρεστιάς "of the mountains" (the formation on ὄρος), no earlier unit has either |
| ἰῷ ἤματι (6.422) | "on one day" | "on a single day" | "in one day", "on the same day"; ἰῷ = ἑνί |
| Ἄϊδος εἴσω (6.422) | "into Hades" | "to the house of Hades" | "to the realm of Hades", "to the underworld"; the house is understood, as in the Odyssey's "gates of Hades" (14.156) |
| βουσὶν ἐπ’ εἰλιπόδεσσι καὶ ἀργεννῇς ὀΐεσσι (6.424) | "rolling-gaited cattle and white sheep" | "cattle of rolling gait and white sheep" | "shambling", "slow-footed"; follows the Odyssey table's εἰλίποδας ἕλικας βοῦς "rolling-gaited … cattle", ἀργεννός "white", ὄϊς "sheep" |
| βασίλευεν (6.425) | "was queen" | "was queen" | "ruled", "reigned", "was king"; βασιλεύω "be king / queen" |
| βάλ’ Ἄρτεμις ἰοχέαιρα (6.428) | "Artemis, the arrow-pourer, hit her" | "Artemis, who showers her arrows, hit her" | "struck her down", "shot her", "smote"; βάλλω of a weapon is "hit" (3.368), Ἄρτεμις ἰοχέαιρα (5.53), and the note says the sense is that she died |
| παρακοίτης θαλερός (6.430) | "a flourishing consort" | "my flourishing husband" | "bedfellow" (an etymology), "spouse", "blooming husband"; masculine of παράκοιτις "consort" / "wife" (4.60), θαλερός of persons "flourishing" (4.474) |
| παῖδ’ ὀρφανικὸν … χήρην τε γυναῖκα (6.432) | "the child an orphan … a woman a widow" | "your son an orphan … your wife a widow" | "fatherless", "orphaned" · "widowed"; the two predicates kept as nouns |
| ἐρινεόν (6.433) | "wild fig-tree" | "wild fig-tree" | "fig-tree" alone (loses the wildness), "caprifig"; ἐρινεός is the wild fig |
| ἀμβατός … ἐπίδρομον (6.434) | "scalable" … "open to assault" | "can best be scaled" … "open to assault" | "climbable", "accessible", "easy to storm"; ἀναβατός "that can be climbed", ἐπίδρομος "that can be run up to" |
| ἐπειρήσανθ’ (6.435) | "made trial" | "made trial of the wall" | "attacked", "tested", "probed"; πειράομαι keeps "make trial" (2.73) |
| ἀμφί + accusative (6.436–437) | "around" | "gathered around" | "led by", "with", "under"; ἀμφί "around", the leaders named with their followers understood |
| ἤ πού τίς … ἔνισπε (6.438) | "Either doubtless someone told them" | "has doubtless told them" | "perhaps", "I suppose", "somewhere" (turned down at που, 3.308); ἐνέπω "tell" (Odyssey ἔννεπε, 2.761) |
| θεοπροπίων ἐῢ εἰδώς (6.438) | "well knowing the prophecies" | "who knew the prophecies well" | "an expert in prophecy", "a seer"; θεοπρόπιον "prophecy" (1.385), εὖ εἰδώς "knew … well" (2.718) |
